intro: Mongolia was the heart of the largest land empire in history, founded by Genghis Khan in 1206. Many Mongolians still live as nomadic herders.

chapters.title: Peoples of the steppe
text: Nomadic peoples like the Xiongnu raided China so often that the Chinese built walls against them. Dinosaur fossils, including the first known dinosaur eggs, have been found in the Gobi.

chapters.title: The Mongol Empire
text: In 1206 Temüjin united the Mongol tribes and took the title Genghis Khan. His horse archers conquered northern China, Central Asia and Persia. Under his heirs the empire stretched from Korea to Hungary.
His grandson Kublai Khan conquered all of China and founded the Yuan dynasty. The empire also linked East and West, helping trade and ideas flow along the Silk Road.

highlight.title: Biggest land empire
highlight.text: At its height the Mongol Empire covered about 24 million km², larger than any other land empire.

chapters.title: Qing, Soviets and democracy
text: The Qing dynasty of China ruled Mongolia from the 1600s. Mongolia declared independence in 1911 and in 1924 became a communist state closely tied to the Soviet Union; thousands of monks were killed in purges in the 1930s.
In 1990 peaceful protests brought multi-party democracy.

keyTerms.meaning: The Mongolian word for a yurt.
